draft.title: Molecules and compounds
card: Molecule
Two or more atoms joined together. The atoms can be of the same element or of different elements.
Compound
A substance made of atoms of different elements joined together in a fixed ratio. Water is a compound: its atoms are always hydrogen and oxygen in the same ratio.
Mixture
Two or more substances mixed together without being joined. The amounts can vary, and the parts keep their own properties. Salty water is a mixture, and you can make it as salty as you like.
Oxygen gas is made of molecules with two oxygen atoms each. It is a molecule but not a compound, because both atoms are the same element.
draft.remember: A compound has different elements joined in a fixed ratio. A mixture is not joined, and its amounts can change.

a.q: Which of these is a compound?
opts: Carbon dioxide, with carbon and oxygen atoms joined
Air, with oxygen and nitrogen gases mixed together
Oxygen gas, with two oxygen atoms joined
Salty water, with salt dissolved in water
a.why: Carbon dioxide has atoms of two different elements joined in a fixed ratio. Oxygen gas has joined atoms, so it is a molecule, but both atoms are the same element, so it is not a compound.
a.clue: A compound needs different elements joined together.

b.q: Sam says that every molecule is a compound. Why is Sam wrong?
opts: A molecule can have atoms of just one element
A molecule can have atoms that are not joined
A molecule can have atoms in any ratio you like
A molecule can have atoms of only two elements
b.why: A molecule is two or more atoms joined, and they can be the same element, as in oxygen gas, which has two oxygen atoms. A compound needs different elements, so some molecules are not compounds.
b.clue: Think about a molecule of oxygen gas.

a.best: Carbon dioxide, with carbon and oxygen atoms joined

b.best: A molecule can have atoms of just one element

problems.detail: "Oxygen gas ... It is a molecule" calls the gas itself a molecule. Oxygen gas is a substance made of many O2 molecules, so this blurs particle and substance. Why (a) repeats it ("so it is a molecule"). Better: "Each oxygen molecule is a molecule but not a compound" or "Oxygen gas is made of molecules but is not a compound."

check.summary: Both questions are correct, with one clear answer each. The only problem is minor wording: the card and why (a) say oxygen gas "is a molecule" when it is made of molecules.
